tagline.text: The northern Bohol port for the Bongan sandbar and the Danajon double barrier reef

location.label: Location
location.text: Northern coast of Bohol Island, a port town facing the Camotes Sea (about 115 km by road from Tagbilaran)

tags.label: Tags

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,200~3,500 (per person, 1 night 2 days from Tagbilaran including transport, boat, entrance fees and meals)

children.text: Talibon is a port town on Bohol's northern coast, close to the Bongan sandbar, 20 to 30 minutes away by boat, and to Danajon Bank, the Philippines' only double barrier reef. It is a quiet northern destination where you can combine the coral-block Blessed Trinity Cathedral with the Carlos P. Garcia memorial park.

Talibon is a first-class municipality on the northern coast of Bohol Island. It borders Bien Unido to the east, Trinidad to the south and Getafe to the west, with the Camotes Sea to the north. According to Wikipedia its area is 140.46 square kilometers and its 2024 population is 71,450, the second largest in Bohol after Ubay. Of its 25 barangays, 17 are on the mainland and 8 are on islands, and island communities such as Nocnocan, Calituban and Guindacpan are described as among the most densely populated islands in the world. The town center sits at only about 7 m above sea level on a low coastal plain. The economy centers on farming and fishing, with rice, corn, copra, bananas, seafood, seaweed and cacao farming, and fishponds. Quarrying of silica, limestone, sand and iron ore, shipped to Cebu and Iligan, is also a major industry.

There are three main ways to reach Talibon. From Tagbilaran it is about 115 km via the western exit of the Bohol Circumferential Road and about 150 km via the eastern exit, and the interior route through Loboc is about 109 km. General guides say it takes almost 3 hours by bus or van. From Cebu there is a ferry to Talibon port, and you can also come overland via Getafe or Tubigon. Most visitors spend a night in Talibon and hire a boat in the morning to reach the Bongan sandbar, and the sea in front of it is Danajon Bank, the only double barrier reef in the Philippines.

Local historian Fr. Jose Maria Luengo wrote that Talibon's history goes back to 1521, saying that survivors of Magellan's ship Trinidad reached the area after Magellan's death. In 1830 it separated from Inabanga to become an independent town, and in 1831 it became a parish dedicated to the Most Holy Trinity. Construction of the stone church began in 1852 and finished in 1899, and it was renovated in 1957 under President Carlos P. Garcia. Japanese troops arrived in June 1942, and in 1947 fifteen barrios were separated to form Trinidad. The Diocese of Talibon was created in 1986, making this church its cathedral. Carlos P. Garcia, the eighth president of the Philippines, was born in this town, and boxer Nonito Donaire and Archbishop Bernardito Auza are also counted among people associated with it. The Trinity feast is celebrated on the last Saturday of May.

The sights are split between the sea and the town. Blessed Trinity Cathedral (Talibon Cathedral) is built of coral blocks on an elevated plain overlooking the sea, and the Carlos P. Garcia monument and park honor the former president. The Bongan sandbar is known for swimming, snorkeling and scuba diving with white sand and clear water, and the Ipil River is said to offer boating, kayaking, fishing and shell gathering, with wild ducks, herons and egrets to see. The San Isidro mangroves are home to monkeys and keep some old mangrove trees. The Danajon Bank marine area is managed jointly by this town and nine neighboring towns, and Talibon is said to have an interpretive center with a 3D model of the reef. A coastal road from the Poblacion port area to Barangay San Francisco is also recorded as having opened in 2026. Danajon Bank is a reef zone about 156 km long and about 272 square kilometers in area, with 40 islands and about 699 km of coastline, crossed by three passes: the Northwest, Middle and Northeast. It has 34 designated marine protected areas, and life such as parrotfish, wrasses, anemonefish, sea fans and seahorses is known there. The reef islands belonging to Talibon include Cataban, Calituban, Guindacpan and Nocnocan. However, overfishing and dynamite fishing have badly damaged the coral habitat, and in 2022 the Bohol government and national agencies created the Bohol Danajon Bank Double Barrier Reef Management Council to deal with protection, food security and ecotourism together. So when choosing a boat or tour operator on this sea, it is wise to check that they follow the rules.

A sandbar 20 to 30 minutes by boat from Talibon port. You can swim and snorkel in white sand and clear sea. It cannot be reached by land, so you must hire a boat at the port. Entrance and environmental fees have changed over the years.

The Philippines' only double barrier reef, one of only six in the world. It is about 156 km long, and several Bohol towns sit on its management council. You can see it on boat tours or dives, so check the management rules before choosing an operator.
The main church of the Diocese of Talibon, built of coral blocks. Construction began in 1852 and was completed in 1899, and it stands on high ground overlooking the sea. Visit quietly during Mass.
A monument and park honoring the eighth president, a native of Talibon. It is a good place to rest while walking around town.

children.text: The mangrove forest is said to be home to monkeys, and on the Ipil River you can watch birds by kayak or boat. Ask the municipal tourism office about how to visit and whether a guide is available.
A facility with a 3D model of Danajon Bank is said to be here. Check opening hours locally.
A coastal road opened in 2026, running from the port area in town to San Francisco, where you can walk with views of the town skyline and the Camotes Sea.

Talibon is best for sea trips in the dry season from December to May. Boat tours to the sandbar and Danajon Bank are best in the morning when the wind is light, so an early start is recommended. On days with bad weather the boats may not go out.

According to modeled climate data, annual rainfall is about 1,326 mm, with April the driest month (about 71 mm) and November the wettest (about 174 mm). Average daily highs are about 29°C and lows are about 24°C.

Talibon town has small guesthouses and homestays. Reliable up-to-date information on prices and facilities is limited, so it is better to book before you arrive. The town is small, and most travelers choose lodging close to the port.

The local area code is 038, the postal code is 6325 and electricity is supplied by the BOHECO 2 cooperative. You can check events and contacts on the municipality's official website (talibon-bohol.gov.ph). Talibon is a working port that mixes industries such as quarrying, seaweed and cacao farming, so it feels less like a tourist spot and more like a look at everyday life in northern Bohol, and its tourist facilities are modest.

Seafood is the main food. You can try grilled dishes and soups near the port and at the market. There are no shops on the sandbar, so bring lunch and water. Check reviews before settling on a particular restaurant.
The Bongan sandbar cannot be reached by land. Hire a boat at the port.
